entities.summary: Chen Wu (b. 200 CE, China) was a public servant or civil administrator of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in China. He played a crucial role in the Han Dynasty's military campaigns against the Xiongnu confederation. Chen Wu's leadership was instrumental in the defeat of the Xiongnu, securing China's northern borders and expanding the empire's influence. His military successes were recognized by Emperor Ling of Han, who awarded him the title of Marquis of Hebei. Chen Wu's legacy extended beyond his military prowess, as he also played a key role in the development of China's administrative systems and infrastructure. The historian Sima Qian, who served under Chen Wu, would later write that 'Chen Wu was a man of great intelligence and military prowess, who made significant contributions to the Han Dynasty's conquests.' The historian's words capture Chen Wu's enduring impact on Chinese history, as he remains one of the most fascinating figures of the Classical era.
